facts.statement: The genus Hemiprotosuchus was named in 1969 by the paleontologist José Bonaparte.
facts.quote: It was named in 1969 by paleontologist José Bonaparte .

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Hemiprotosuchus leali.
facts.quote: The type species is H. leali.

facts.statement: Hemiprotosuchus lived during the Late Triassic (Norian stage) in the Los Colorados Formation of northwestern Argentina.
facts.quote: Hemiprotosuchus is an extinct genus of protosuchid crocodyliform from the Late Triassic (Norian stage) Los Colorados Formation of the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin in northwestern Argentina, South America.

facts.statement: A 2009 cladistic analysis determined that Hemiprotosuchus is the sister taxon of Protosuchus.
facts.quote: A 2009 cladistic analysis of protosuchids by paleontologist Eric Buffetaut et al. found that Hemiprotosuchus was the sister taxon of Protosuchus.

facts.statement: The known fossils of Hemiprotosuchus include a skull, jaws, and some postcranial elements.
facts.quote: The fossils included a skull and jaws as well as some postcranial elements.

facts.statement: Hemiprotosuchus belongs to the family Protosuchidae.
Hemiprotosuchus lived between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago during the Norian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)
